glm.feedback:
## Findings

- Category: spec
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeedCard.tsx / mission-chat.css (whole diff)
  Finding: The spec explicitly says "NO error messages" in the chat, but nothing in the diff addresses suppression of error content (error tool_results, transient errors, failing-card error prose). The diff only touches rejected AskUserQuestion handling; other error-rendering paths appear untouched.
  Suggestion: Verify how error tool_results / error-status cards render in the new style; either hide them or render them as the small grey tool lines, and add a test covering an errored tool call.

- Category: spec
  Severity: low
  File: client/e2e/flows/M5-mission-desktop-chat.spec.ts:139-142 and MissionAskCards.tsx
  Finding: Spec says "Unanswered questions are not shown", but a pending (never-answered, never-rejected) question is still shown with its Answer CTA. The diff treats "unanswered" as "answered-with-blank/rejected", which may be the intended FR-01.63 CTA preservation, but it contradicts the literal spec sentence.
  Suggestion: Confirm with spec owner whether "unanswered" means "no result line yet" (then pending questions must be hidden) or only blank answers; adjust code or spec wording.

- Category: regression
  Severity: medium
  File: client/src/components/external/mission/MissionActivityFeedCard.tsx:13 (`export { kindAccent } from "./MissionActivityFeedCardParts"` removed)
  Finding: `kindAccent` was a public export of both `MissionActivityFeedCardParts` and `MissionActivityFeedCard`; both are now deleted. Any out-of-diff consumer (other components, snapshot/storybook files, or tests importing it) will fail to compile.
  Suggestion: Grep the repo for `kindAccent` before merge; if any consumer remains, keep the export or migrate that consumer in this change.

- Category: bug
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/missionActivityFeedResolve.ts:89-92 (rejected-card splice)
  Finding: Splicing a card out of `cards` shifts the indices used in the React key `${card.kind}-${timestamp}-${commands[0]}-${index}` in `MissionActivityFeed.tsx`, remounting every later card in the feed (loss of expand/collapse state, scroll jank on large feeds). Also, if the rejected card is the one holding `feed` narration (text assigned to the user-input card via own-prose routing), that narration disappears too.
  Suggestion: Prefer marking the card as hidden (a flag the feed filters on) rather than mutating the shared array, and confirm narration text never lives on a user-input card that can be rejected.

- Category: edge-case
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/missionAskItems.ts:70-75 (`applyAskAnswers` keyed by exact question text)
  Finding: The join is an exact string match on question text. Claude's `toolUseResult.answers` keys can differ in whitespace/case from the tool_use input's `question`; any mismatch silently makes the question "unanswered" and it disappears from the feed (filtered by `i.answer !== undefined`). Also, `answers[item.question]` accesses an arbitrary untrusted key — fine for reads, but note `raw` values are rendered verbatim (React escapes, so no XSS).
  Suggestion: Consider a normalized (trimmed) key lookup as a fallback when the exact key misses, so a whitespace difference doesn't drop an answered question.

- Category: test
  Severity: low
  File: client/src/lib/missionAskItems.ts:71 (`seen` duplicate-question handling)
  Finding: Duplicate question texts: first occurrence wins, later duplicates stay unanswered and are filtered out — but only the unit test asserts `dup).toHaveLength(1)` without asserting which one or that answers went to the right one. Minor: acceptable, but the filter means a legitimately repeated question (same text, two cards in one call) loses its second answer entirely.
  Suggestion: Acceptable as a documented limitation; consider rendering the answer on all duplicates of that text instead of only the first.

Everything else — sidecar trust guarded by `results.length === 1`, rejection path, legacy fallback, multi-result sidecar ignore, and the no-bubble CSS ordering — is correct and well-tested. The unit tests are behavioral (assert chosen/other/multi-select/rejected/pending states through the real reducer), not smoke tests.

Overall: the core rendering and parsing logic is sound and well covered; fix the `kindAccent` export removal (compile risk) and clarify the "unanswered/pending" and "NO error messages" spec points before shipping. Ship-with-fixes.

SHIPWRIGHT_VERDICT: revise
